question: Using primary SQLite documentation, explain how to detect FTS5 support at runtime and what guarantees or limitations apply to external-content FTS5 tables.

claims.text: `PRAGMA module_list` can be used as a connection-level runtime check for FTS5 availability, because it returns registered virtual-table modules and FTS5 is a virtual-table module; if `fts5` appears there, FTS5 is available on that connection at that moment.
acceptable_patterns: FTS5 is an SQLite virtual-?table module

evidence_passages.text: `PRAGMA module_list;` returns the list of virtual-table modules registered with the current database connection. FTS5 is an SQLite virtual-table module.

`[Inference]` If `fts5` appears in `PRAGMA module_list`, FTS5 is available on that connection at that moment; this follows from “module_list returns registered virtual-table modules” plus “FTS5 is a virtual-table module.”

claims.text: Compile-option introspection can detect a built-in FTS5 build: `PRAGMA compile_options` returns compile-time options without the `SQLITE_` prefix, so the relevant row is `ENABLE_FTS5`, and `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` or SQL `sqlite_compileoption_used()` report whether a named compile-time option was used.
acceptable_patterns: SQLITE_ prefix is omitted|omits the `SQLITE_` prefix

evidence_passages.text: `PRAGMA compile_options;` returns the compile-time options used to build SQLite, one per row, and omits the `SQLITE_` prefix.
`SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` adds FTS5 to the build automatically when that option is defined for the amalgamation build.
In C, `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` returns `0` or `1` depending on whether a named compile-time option was defined, and the `SQLITE_` prefix may be omitted when calling that C API.
In SQL, `sqlite_compileoption_used()` is a wrapper around `sqlite3_compileoption_used()`.

claims.text: An external-content FTS5 table uses `content=` to name a table, virtual table, or view in the same database, and `content_rowid=` can override the default rowid column name used by FTS5.

evidence_passages.text: `[Supported fact]` An external-content FTS5 table is created by setting `content=` to the name of a table, virtual table, or view in the same database; `content_rowid=` can override the default rowid column name used by FTS5.

claims.text: For external-content tables, SQLite documents full FTS5 functionality, but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; otherwise query results may be unpredictable.
acceptable_patterns: all FTS5 functionality may be used

evidence_passages.text: `[Supported fact]` With external content, “all FTS5 functionality may be used,” but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; if not, query results may be unpredictable.

claims.text: External-content query behavior depends on whether the full-text index is used: without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, SQLite effectively passes the query through to the content table; with the full-text index, FTS5 first gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up the corresponding column values in the content table.
acceptable_patterns: passes? .* through to the content table
first gets matching rowids from the index
looks up .* in the content table

evidence_passages.text: `[Supported fact]` If a query against the external-content FTS5 table does not use the full-text index, such as one without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, SQLite effectively passes that query through to the content table, so the FTS index does not affect the result.
`[Supported fact]` If a query does use the full-text index, FTS5 first gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up the corresponding column values in the content table.

claims.text: Triggers are a documented synchronization method for external-content FTS5 tables, but creating them after the content table already has rows does not backfill the index; if the index and content table become inconsistent, the documented `rebuild` command can discard and rebuild the FTS index from the current content table.
acceptable_patterns: does not backfill|does not backfill the FTS index

evidence_passages.text: `[Supported fact]` Triggers are one documented way to keep an external-content FTS5 table synchronized with its content table.
`[Supported fact]` Creating those triggers after the content table already contains rows does not backfill the FTS index; the triggers only keep later inserts, updates, and deletes synchronized.
`[Supported fact]` If the FTS index and content table become inconsistent, the documented `rebuild` command can discard the existing FTS index and rebuild it from the current content table.

claims.text: External-content FTS5 tables do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling; operations that specify `REPLACE` are handled using `ABORT`.

evidence_passages.text: `[Supported fact]` External-content FTS5 tables do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling; operations that specify `REPLACE` are handled using `ABORT`.

rejected_claims.text: `sqlite3_compileoption_used("SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5")` alone proves that FTS5 is available on the current connection.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by supplied evidence that FTS5 may be a loadable extension and that compile-option checks do not by themselves prove current connection-level registration.

rejected_claims.text: SQLite automatically keeps an external-content FTS5 index synchronized with its content table.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by supplied evidence stating the user is responsible for consistency and that triggers are only one documented synchronization method.

rejected_claims.text: Creating synchronization triggers after populating the content table backfills existing rows into the FTS index.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by supplied evidence stating trigger creation does not backfill the FTS index.

rejected_claims.text: External-content FTS5 tables support `REPLACE` conflict handling normally.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by supplied evidence stating `REPLACE` is handled using `ABORT`.

rejected_claims.text: SQLite primary documentation provides a dedicated single-purpose API specifically documented as 'detect whether FTS5 is available now on this connection'.
rejected_claims.reason: Supplied evidence explicitly says no dedicated single-purpose API was found beyond module introspection, compile-option introspection, and extension loading.

rejected_claims.text: Compile-option checks do not by themselves prove that FTS5 is currently registered on a specific connection, because FTS5 may be built as a loadable extension and extension loading is disabled by default until enabled with `sqlite3_enable_load_extension()`.
rejected_claims.reason: Le concept requis 'disabled_by_default' et les motifs 'extension loading is disabled by default' / 'sqlite3_enable_load_extension()' ne sont appuyés que par les evidence_passages du run Codex, qui recopient sa propre réponse finale (opened_urls vide, aucun payload d'outil exposé) — support circulaire. La récupération de lang_corefunc.html dans le run Claude ne documente que sqlite_compileoption_get/used, sans mention de load_extension. La partie corroborée (FTS5 disponible en extension chargeable, donc test d'option de compilation insuffisant au niveau connexion) est déjà couverte par c1 et c2.
